bio: Sebastian Dows-Miller is a Research Fellow at University College London, supported by the Leverhulme Trust. In his research, he applies digital methods to the study of manuscripts written in French, asking what we can learn about medieval scribes from how they abbreviate words. He also recently published an open-access book on the œuvre of Jehan de Saint-Quentin, in which he uses statistical techniques to shed light on this case of uncertain authorship.

Jin Gao a Lecturer in Digital Archives at the UCL Department of Information Studies, the Acting Programme Director for the MA/MSc in Digital Humanities programmes, Co-Director at the UCL Centre for Digital Humanities. She is also a Research Fellow at the Victoria and Albert (V&A) Museum leading on collaborative research projects, e.g., Chinese Export Watercolours (CEW), Computer and Digital Art Network (CDAN), and Stein Textiles Reconstruction and Analysis Project (STRAP) projects.

Barbara McGillivray is Senior Lecturer in Digital and Computational Humanities in the Department of Digital Humanities of King’s College, where she leads the Computational Humanities research group. She is Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Open Humanities Data and convenor of the MA programme in Digital Humanities at King’s. Her research focuses on computational methods for the study of language change in both historical languages and contemporary data.

Rachele Rosina is a PhD student at King’s College London, combining computer vision and archival research to examine how places are photographed and perceived at scale. Her interests include the politics of digital archives, decolonising cultural heritage data and bias in AI. She holds an MA in East Asian History of Art from SOAS and a double BA in Chinese Language and Culture from Ca’ Foscari University of Venice and CNU, Beijing.

Anna Zakharova is a PhD student in the Department of Information Studies at University College London (UCL). Her research applies computational text analysis and quantitative methods to examine how gender is depicted in child-directed media, situating her work within the Digital Humanities. She is also an Associate Director (PhD) of the UCL Centre for Digital Humanities (UCLDH), a role dedicated to supporting the centre’s postgraduate research community.

Caitlin is a PhD candidate in Digital Humanities, holding a UKRI scholarship from the London Arts & Humanities Partnership (LAHP). She is working on a Collaborative Doctoral Award with The National Archives, working with their Find Case Law service. She holds an undergraduate degree in Linguistics from the University of Edinburgh and a MSc in Digital Scholarship from the University of Oxford. She has also trained as a Digital Archivist at the UK Parliamentary Archives.
